messages:
devon: spotting elevated PodPending in ord1 GPU pool, many PVs stuck at AttachInProgress. Kube events show timeouts to the cloud attach API.

maria: confirmed — 25% of gpu-serving nodes show disk attach failures over last 3m, autoscaler is thrashing trying to replace nodes.

alice: trend looks like a control-plane / cloud API rate-limit vs network egress. I can still ping metadata endpoints from a node, but attach API calls are returning 503s intermittently.

sam (oncall): paging cloud provider now, filing support ticket. Incident lead: devon.

patrick: starting traffic shift plan: move canary jobs off ord1 to us-west2 and drain 12 nodes. We should prefer moving latency-insensitive batch first.

devon: agreed. maria, can you trigger node-drain for the oldest nodes only and pause autoscaler? We don't want new scale attempts against failing attach calls.

maria: pausing autoscaler policy for ord1, running:
```bash
kubectl label nodes gpu-ord1-* node.kubernetes.io/drain-candidate=true
kubectl cordon gpu-ord1-03
kubectl drain gpu-ord1-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
Drain in progress, 3 pods failed to relocate due to PV attachment errors.

devon: workaround suggestion: for the batch pool we can mount ephemeral NVMe and use cached weights (no PV attach). Will cost more if we fall back to ephemeral, but keeps throughput. Thoughts?

alice: yes we can switch the batch stack to ephemeral with a fast init image. I’ll prepare a patch to the job template to use emptyDir + init container to wget weights from our cache-bucket.

sam (oncall): rolling this to batch first. notify infra-bot to start traffic-shift doc and update status page.

infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — ord1 persistent storage attach errors. Severity: P2. Affected: Dedicated GPU pools (batch & some serving fallbacks). Current mitigations: autoscaler paused, draining nodes, batch work switched to ephemeral mounts.

patrick: cost note — ephemeral fallback will increase egress and storage transfer costs; estimate +$2.5k/day if we keep this for 24h at current batch volume. Logging that for finance.

maria: cloud support responded: "We are investigating an internal controller causing attach API throttling in ord1. Root-cause under review. ETA unknown." They recommended retry/backoff; but our attach attempts are already aggressive and causing pressure.

devon: okay, new plan: 1) stop automated node replacements in ord1 2) drain only healthy nodes to reduce pod pressure 3) for serving traffic, shift 30% to us-west2 routing via traffic-mgr 4) batch -> ephemeral 5) keep KMS usage local (no cross-region KMS calls)

alice: changing routing:
```json
{
  "route": "inference-service",
  "weights": { "ord1": 70, "us-west2": 30 },
  "constraints": ["latency < 250ms for ord1" ]
}
```
Applying now.

sam (oncall): applied. Monitoring latency and error rates.

infra-bot: METRICS — ord1 attach error rate down from 18% -> 11% after throttle and drains. Request latency for attach endpoint still elevated.

patrick: ops question — do we want to trigger Dedicated overprovision (burst extra reserved GPUs) in us-west2? We have some burst capacity but need approval. Cost is ~ $6k/day.

devon: not yet. Wait to see stability in ord1 for 1h. If attach errors persist >15% after 1h we open reserved capacity.

alice: also found a failing kubelet log sample:
```
E0301 12:03:17 kubelet_volumes.go:123] attach failed: failed to attach volume "pvc-abc123" to node: error attaching volume: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
```
This matches provider-side gRPC errors.

maria: successful workaround for 2 pods: recreated them with ephemeral mount + weights pulled at init. They started serving in ~45s.

sam (oncall): status page updated: "Partial storage attach degradation in ord1 — mitigations in progress. Some serving and batch traffic routed away."

devon: escalation note — if provider confirms control-plane issue lasting >4h we should plan for a region failover for customer-critical serving (A/B canary to us-west2 then full cutover). Start drafting communication templates.

patrick: drafting cost and runbook now, will post in #incidents-daily.

infra-bot: Cloud Support update pushed by maria: "Iterator controller causing attach throttles; mitigation deploying in 15-30m. Monitoring recommended after rollout."

alice: once provider finishes rollout, we should gradually restore PV-based workloads with a cautious attach rate (1 attach/sec per availability zone) and monitor attach errors. Add a circuit-breaker to scale slower.

maria: provider reports mitigation rolled out. I’ll resume autoscaler with a conservative min and attach rate limiter in place.

infra-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVE CHECKLIST: autoscaler resumed w/ rate limits, drained nodes reprovisioned, batch jobs returned to PV after validation, cost impact estimate captured. Closing incident in 30m if no regressions. :white_check_mark:

devon: great work. Postmortem owners: devon (infra), maria (ops), alice (platform). Please capture timeline, cost impact, and a proposal to add client-side exponential backoff + jitter in attach path.

sam (oncall): ack. Closing the incident thread once postmortem draft is shared.
